definitions.gloss: good omen; auspicious sign; lucky sign
definitions.explanation: A sign or event believed to foretell something good. Used in both traditional and modern contexts.

examples.japanese: {虹|にじ}は{吉兆|きっちょう}とされている。
examples.english: Rainbows are considered a good omen.

examples.japanese: {新年|しんねん}に{鶴|つる}を{見|み}るのは{吉兆|きっちょう}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Seeing a crane on New Year's is said to be an auspicious sign.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}から{天気|てんき}がよく、{何|なに}か{吉兆|きっちょう}のような{気|き}がした。
examples.english: The weather was fine from morning, and it felt like some kind of good omen.

notes:
{吉兆|きっちょう} combines {吉|きち} (good fortune) + {兆|ちょう} (sign, omen). A somewhat literary or formal word for an auspicious sign.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {吉兆|きっちょう}とされる (to be considered a good omen)
- {吉兆|きっちょう}の{兆|きざ}し (signs of a good omen)
- {吉兆|きっちょう}と{見|み}なす (to regard as a good sign)

TRADITIONAL GOOD OMENS IN JAPAN:
- {鶴|つる} (cranes) — longevity and good fortune
- {虹|にじ} (rainbows) — bridges between worlds
- {初夢|はつゆめ}に{富士山|ふじさん} (Mt. Fuji in first dream of the year)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {凶兆|きょうちょう}: bad omen (direct antonym)
- {縁起|えんぎ}がいい: auspicious, lucky (everyday equivalent)
- {吉|きち}: good fortune (used in {占|うらな}い/fortune-telling: {大吉|だいきち}, {中吉|ちゅうきち})

REGISTER:
More formal/literary than {縁起|えんぎ}がいい. Common in written language and cultural contexts.
